newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zairean opposition opposes foreign intervention.
newsitem.headline: Zairean opposition opposes foreign intervention.

text.p: A Zairean opposition party urged France on Monday to reject plans for foreign intervention in a spreading rebel war in eastern Zaire, calling instead for a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

"The Union for Democracy and Social Progress calls on the French government to reject plans for foreign intervention in Zaire, as called for by Kamanda Wa Kamanda, foreign minister for the mafia-politico-military power in Kinshasa," the UDPS said in a statement issued by its representative in Paris.

"The UDPS prefers a peaceful solution of the coflict in eastern Zaire and urges above all a national unity government under the leadership of (main radical opposition leader) Etienne Tshisekedi," the party said.

A senior Zaire defence ministry official said on Monday that Zaire has chartered planes to bring in troops from African allies Morocco, Togo and Chad to help its army in the rebel war in the eastern part of the central African state,
The official said that Egypt had offered equipment to equip the infantry.
The official could not give a definite date for the arrival of the foreign troops.

Tutsi-led rebels battling the mercenary-backed Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba Province.

The rebel leaders say their objective is to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko who has ruled Zaire since 1965, while Mobutu has vowed to defeat the rebels on the battlefield and ruled out negotiations.

Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting along with the ethnic Tutsis who launched an armed rebellion after local authorities threatened to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda.
